subject.title: [OAuth] Client ID revoked `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` - fresh ChatGPT Plus logins completely broken

question: Should OpenClaw rotate the built-in ChatGPT/Codex OAuth client ID now, keep the current upstream-aligned client and steer users to device-code/API-key fallback, or wait for maintainer-owned fresh-browser repro before changing source?
rationale: The code change is small only after the OAuth app owner and supported flow are chosen; a blind constant swap could desynchronize OpenClaw from upstream Codex and break device-code or refresh paths.

options.title: Verify, then rotate official client
options.body: A maintainer with OAuth app ownership should reproduce the fresh-browser failure, register or confirm the replacement client, and update browser, device-code, refresh, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Keep current client with fallback
options.body: Leave the upstream-aligned client ID in place and make device-code pairing or API-key login the supported recovery while collecting browser proof.

options.title: Defer until reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but avoid source changes until a fresh account screenshot, recording, or logs show the invalid-client response after Cloudflare/browser checks.

recommendation.title: Verify, then rotate official client
recommendation.body: A maintainer with OAuth app ownership should reproduce the fresh-browser failure, register or confirm the replacement client, and update browser, device-code, refresh, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history signal for the current OpenAI provider identity and auth surface, and the decision needs provider/auth ownership context.
